articles.title: Comment des hackers ont pu se faire passer pour Google en piratant trois extensions nationales
articles.summary:
C’est une campagne cybercriminelle d’une ampleur rare que vient de dévoiler Google le 6 octobre 2026.
Et pour cause, elle ne vise pas un site ou une entreprise en particulier, mais directement les registres de trois extensions nationales, le .gh du Ghana, le .sl de la Sierra Leone et le .as des Samoa américaines.
Ces organismes tiennent l’annuaire de tous les noms de domaine qui se terminent par leur extension, et indiquent, à travers le système DNS, vers quel serveur un nom doit renvoyer lorsqu’un internaute le saisit dans son navigateur.
En prenant la main sur ces registres, les attaquants ont donc pu rediriger n’importe quel domaine en .gh, .sl ou .as, quel que soit le niveau de sécurité de son propriétaire. Or, comme de nombreuses multinationales, Google possède des déclinaisons locales de ses sites dans ces extensions.
De vrais certificats pour de faux sites
En piratant les registres, les attaquants ont ainsi pu modifier les informations officielles qui indiquent vers quel serveur pointent ces domaines, puis demander des certificats HTTPS.
Ces certificats, délivrés par des autorités de certification, sont ceux qui permettent au navigateur d’afficher le cadenas et de garantir à l’internaute qu’il communique avec le bon site.
Avant d’en délivrer un, l’autorité vérifie que le demandeur contrôle bien le domaine, le plus souvent en passant par le DNS. Comme les attaquants contrôlaient justement le DNS, ils ont passé cette vérification sans difficulté et obtenu des certificats…

articles.title: Microsoft Outlook to block MSIX attachments starting November
articles.summary:
Microsoft announced that it will add .msix and .msixbundle attachments to the list of blocked attachments in Outlook Web and the new Outlook Windows client starting next month.
.msix files are modern Windows installation packages tailored for specific computer architectures or configurations, while .msixbundle is a container that groups multiple .msix packages into a single file compatible with multiple computer architectures.
The change will begin rolling out to Exchange Online users in early November, when the new file types will be added to the BlockedFileTypes list in all OWA Mailbox policies, and is expected to reach general availability by mid-November.
After the policies are updated, .msix or .msixbundle attachments will be blocked by default, and users of Outlook on the web and new Outlook for Windows will no longer be able to send, receive, open, or download them.
"To enhance security in Outlook on the web and new Outlook for Windows, we are updating the default list of blocked file types in OwaMailboxPolicy," Microsoft said in a Microsoft 365 message center update.
"As part of this update, the .msix and .msixbundle file types will be added to the BlockedFileTypes list in the default OWA Mailbox policy and any custom policies created in your tenant."

articles.title: Canada is making it easier to build cell towers through new regulations
articles.summary:
Canada is considering changes to the rules governing wireless infrastructure, with today being the deadline for final reply comments.
According to PlanHub, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED) wants to streamline approval of new cell towers. Under this new proposal, local authorities would have 45 days to approve or formally challenge a project. If no action is taken within that window, the tower can be considered approved.
Telecom companies could also be allowed to build cell towers under 15 metres without the standard municipal and public consultation process. ISED is also looking at ways to make small-cell deployment easier, which PlanHub said could matter as carriers densify 5G networks.
Shifting to roaming and tower sharing, ISED has removed the wording requiring carriers to provide roaming only “where technically feasible,” and now requires roaming to be offered upon request when the customer’s device can access the host network.
A similar change will now be applied to tower sharing, as carriers will be required to share antenna sites when requested. Alongside this, technical disputes will move to arbitration instead of being decided directly by the ISED.
The Government of Canada also noted that both tower sharing and mandatory roaming are important, as it can “empower smaller or regional licensees to provide increased choice for Canadians through services and coverage competitive with those offered by the national wireless operators.”

articles.title: The Async Multiprocessing Has Sound Foundations in Linux, But Further Testing Is Needed
articles.summary:
At Embedded Linux Conference Europe 2026, Wolfram Sang, a Linux kernel developer and maintainer of the Linux I2C subsystem, examined the Linux building blocks for asymmetric multiprocessing (AMP). His assessment: they are sound enough to build on, but thin contributor coverage and fragmented testing need attention.
His talk drew on an attempt to upstream a hardware-spinlock driver, work that led him to examine the health of the wider AMP stack. He focused on the Linux side, pointing attendees to other conference talks for Zephyr, trusted firmware and device-tree details.
In a basic AMP system, Linux application CPUs and a smaller real-time core run within the same system-on-chip. A mailbox signals that information is available; shared SRAM or DDR holds the data. More complex systems must also coordinate ownership of shared resources. Sang described SCMI as a way for Linux to communicate with a dedicated system-control processor about resources such as clocks, rather than managing every resource alone.
That communication is less straightforward than a mailbox diagram suggests. A doorbell typically signals in one direction. Sang showed how two unidirectional mailboxes can form one request-and-response channel, while a fully bidirectional SCMI arrangement can require four. articles.title: Qilin Ransomware Suspect Arrested in Japan, Extradited to Germany
articles.summary:
An alleged member of the Qilin ransomware group was arrested in Japan and subsequently extradited to Germany.
The suspect, a 28-year-old Russian national, was detained in Osaka in May and was reportedly handed over to the German authorities on October 2.
Believed to be a core member of the ransomware gang, the individual was wanted in Germany for hacking into a logistics company in September 2024, encrypting data on its systems, and extorting it of over $160,000 in cryptocurrency.
Also known as Agenda, Qilin has been active since August 2022 and has become one of the most prolific ransomware-as-a-service (RaaS) operations, hitting hundreds of organizations worldwide and causing millions of dollars in damages.
In 2024, the group was blamed for hacking into pathology lab services provider Synnovis and causing disruptions at multiple London hospitals run by the National Health Service.
Last year, Qilin claimed responsibility for hacking beer giant Asahi Group. The incident caused operational disruptions and resulted in the personal information of roughly 2 million people being compromised.

articles.title: Hackers hijack Google domains after breaching ccTLD registries
articles.summary:
Hackers obtained unauthorized HTTPS certificates for several Google domains and hijacked domains in the country-code top-level domains (ccTLDs) for Ghana, American Samoa, and Sierra Leone after compromising third-party operators and modifying authoritative DNS records.
Google underlines that the attacks affected domains of other organizations in the .GH, .SL, and .AS ccTLDs but "did not involve a compromise of Google’s systems."
By gaining access to the domain name system (DNS) records, a threat actor can request an HTTPS certificate from a Certificate Authority (CA) for a domain they don't own.
CAs issue certificates after verifying ownership of the domain, a process that typically requires the requester to create a TXT record with a random value the CA provides.
Modifying the authoritative DNS records allowed the threat actor to point .GH, .SL, and .AS domains to infrastructure they controlled while obtaining valid TLS certificates for those domains.
This let the attacker impersonate legitimate brands and serve visitors arbitrary content from the affected domains.
Google immediately blocked the unauthorized certificates for its properties in Chrome through CRLSets and worked with the issuing authorities to revoke them, extending protection to other clients.
The company said that its systems were not affected by the incident in any way, and that it has no reason to believe that the issuing CAs acted improperly.

En mai 2026, Google avait annoncé son intention de faire de SynthID, son filigrane invisible dans les contenus générés par IA, un standard. Gemini, la recherche Google et Chrome peuvent déjà dire si une image contient le filigrane SynthID, avec pour objectif final d’avoir un filigrane unique pour tous les services.
Le 7 octobre 2026, Google annonce le lancement d’un site dédié à la reconnaissance d’images IA : SynthID Detector, accessible à l’adresse synthid.com. Présenté l’an dernier, l’outil était jusqu’ici réservé aux professionnels et aux médias.
Comment fonctionne SynthID Detector ?
SynthID permet d’importer une image, une vidéo ou un fichier audio. L’outil cherche ensuite la présence d’un filigrane SynthID, une signature invisible insérée dans le contenu au moment de sa génération. Selon Google, le filigrane résiste aux recadrages, aux changements de couleur et aux compressions : il est impossible de le supprimer.
En plus des images générées par Nano Banana, SynthID reconnaît les créations OpenAI (dont ChatGPT Images 2.0), NVIDIA et Kakao. Google ajoute qu’Apple rejoindra « bientôt » la liste, sans donner de date. Les rivaux de Google sont plusieurs à avoir accepté la proposition de l’entreprise pour que SynthID devienne la norme.
Un outil utile, mais pas un détecteur universel
Depuis 2023, Google dit que plus de 180 milliards d’images et de vidéos ont été marquées avec un SynthID. Le problème est que SynthID Detector ne peut pas « reconnaître » un contenu IA, mais seul…

articles.title: Survey Finds AI-Generated Code Increases Debugging and Failure Rates and Creates a Comprehension Gap
articles.summary:
A survey conducted by independent research firm Coleman Parkes on behalf of Undo, a company focused on scaling AI-powered root-cause analysis, found that while AI coding agents have accelerated code generation, they have shifted the primary bottleneck to debugging, code comprehension, and maintenance.
The report surveyed 300 senior engineer leaders responsible for delivering mission-critical software, most of whom working with C/C++. The survey focuses specifically on mission-critical codebases where code "must be understood", with respondent identifying the most demanding task as "understanding what that code does, how it affects existing codebases, and debugging it when an application doesn’t behave the way it’s expected to".
In those environments, teams spend an average of 9.8 hours per week producing code, but 16.9 hours per week debugging issues identified during development or encountered by customers in production, accounting for 42% of the average working week.
Along with debugging getting more relevant, another critical dimension is emerging as a challenge, code comprehension:
Now that AI is generating most of the code being produced, engineers no longer have the inherent understanding they used to. That makes it easier for defects to escape, and when something inevitably goes wrong, nobody has the knowledge to trace the failure back to its root cause.

articles.title: ChatGPT keeps signing fake New Yorker cartoons with real artists' names
articles.summary:
WTF?! AI companies have long faced accusations from artists, authors, and researchers that they scrape copyrighted material without permission to train their models. A more recent investigation has found that ChatGPT has not only been generating cartoons that mimic The New Yorker's signature style, but also adding the real signatures of the magazine's cartoonists to the AI-generated work.
According to Nieman Lab, ChatGPT has been producing artwork suspiciously similar in style and content to cartoons previously published in The New Yorker. More troubling, the investigation found that the chatbot added forged signatures from several real cartoonists, which led some viewers to assume humans had drawn the images.
The issue drew wider attention after the death of country music legend Dolly Parton in August, when an AI-generated cartoon of the singer went viral, racking up tens of thousands of likes, shares, and comments. The image shows Parton entering heaven arm-in-arm with British actor Tim Curry, who also died that month.
The cartoon carried the pen name "BLOPER," the signature New Yorker cartoonist Brendan Loper uses on his work. Loper told Nieman Lab he did not draw it. The image was generated by ChatGPT and first posted to Facebook by a Dolly Parton fan who had asked for "a New Yorker-style cartoon."

The Atlanta-based energy holding company serves more than 9 million customers through electric utilities in three states and natural gas distribution businesses in four. Its electric subsidiaries are Georgia Power, Alabama Power and Mississippi Power.
Roughly 300,000 of the affected accounts belong to Georgia Power customers. According to Southern Company, the incident also impacted roughly 100,000 of Alabama Power’s 1.6 million accounts.
Mississippi Power is named as affected in the company’s public notice, but no figure has been released for its customers.
“An unauthorized third party accessed certain, limited information about the accounts of approximately 400K customers. Upon detection, we took immediate steps to stop the activity and have engaged law enforcement,” the company said in a statement sent to the media.
Southern Company’s public notice specifies the type of data involved. “Based on our investigation to date, the limited customer account information that the unauthorized party gained access to includes the customer’s name, mailing address, phone number, email, or the last 4 digits of their Social Security Number, and other basic account details,” the notice reads.
The utility says the attacker did not access bank account numbers, payment card numbers or driver’s license numbers.

Mais ce nouveau protocole ne convient pas à tout le monde et génère parfois des problèmes. Jusqu’à présent, il était possible de désactiver le RCS pour chaque conversation, ce qui permettait de basculer aux bons vieux SMS et MMS dans une conversation. Cette option pourrait bientôt disparaître.
Un réglage pourtant bien pratique
Repérées dans la dernière version bêta de l’application, des lignes de code confirment que Google prépare le terrain en prévenant les utilisateurs que le paramètre pour forcer uniquement l’envoi de SMS et MMS s’apprête à disparaître définitivement. L’application incite ainsi les utilisateurs à basculer dès maintenant vers les discussions enrichies (RCS) ou à laisser la mise à jour s’appliquer automatiquement.
Deux options
Une fois cette modification déployée auprès de tous les utilisateurs de Google Messages, les marges de manœuvre vont se réduire pour ceux qui préfèrent éviter le protocole de Google. Il restera seulement deux alternatives : désactiver totalement la fonction pour l’ensemble des conversations, ou s’en remettre au mécanisme de secours classique qui bascule automatiquement vers les SMS et MMS uniquement lorsque l’envoi du message RCS échoue.

articles.title: FBI: Ongoing FortiBleed attacks lock out FortiGate VPN admins
articles.summary:
The FBI is warning that FortiBleed attacks are still ongoing, targeting exposed Fortinet FortiGate firewalls and SSL VPN gateways and locking out legitimate administrators.
Hackers gain access to exposed endpoints by using previously leaked credentials, or logins obtained from infostealer logs, credential stuffing, and password spraying attacks.
They then extract additional authentication data from compromised devices and use a distributed GPU cluster running Hashcat and Hashtopolis to crack offline the stolen password hashes.
According to the FBI, " the FortiBleed attack chain has been observed as an initial entry point for ransomware affiliates." Some groups benefiting from this are INC/Lynx ransomware and Payload ransomware.
The leak that keeps on giving
FortiBleed is a massive Fortinet credentials leak discovered in June, when attackers inadvertently exposed a server containing usernames and plaintext passwords associated with 73,932 firewall URLs across 194 countries.
The data revealed a large-scale credential-harvesting operation, although it was unclear at the time what method was used to obtain the configuration data.
In July, SOCRadar linked FortiBleed to the INC and Lynx ransomware operations after getting access to both groups’ negotiation panels on a server used in the campaign.
By the SOCRadar's latest count, the FotiBleed compromised 86,644 devices.

Decision models are suddenly everywhere. OpenAI’s is now public.
This week, OpenAI opened its Decisions API to public beta and added image inputs to make fast decisions from visual content.
First announced last week as a likely response to TypeSafe’s Jev, OpenAI is now billing its decision model at $0.10 per 1M input tokens. There are no output-token charges, nor charges for cache reads or writes.
Running on GPT-6 Luna, the public beta version gives all developers the ability to turn text or images into three types of structured outputs: predicates (i.e., how likely something is to be true), choices (i.e., which predefined option is the best fit), and scores (i.e., where an input falls on a numeric range).
But OpenAI’s Decisions API may be but one fish in a sea of decision models. Perplexity, Cloudflare, and Amazon also dropped their own versions this month, opting for open-weight models that developers can download and run on their own infrastructure.
What Decisions API can do with image input
In a new video, OpenAI shows how image inputs can help applications take quick action based on visual understanding.
It offers the example of a video game with a car moving through traffic. Using frames of the road and obstacles, Decisions API can choose whether the car should switch lanes or keep driving.
OpenAI claims its API can make those decisions in a fraction of the time a reasoning model would take to do the same.

articles.title: Fraudster jailed for using 10K bots and AI songs to outstream Taylor Swift
articles.summary:
After pleading guilty, a 54-year-old North Carolina man, Michael Smith, was sentenced to 18 months in prison for using artificial intelligence to generate songs for a scheme that stole millions from music streaming platforms.
In a press release Tuesday, the US Department of Justice said that Smith is the first American criminally charged with AI-assisted streaming fraud.
First charged in 2024, Smith successfully ran the scheme for seven years without detection.
Starting in 2017, Smith began using fake email accounts and “fraudulently obtained debit cards” to create “thousands of fraudulent accounts” on services including Amazon Music, Apple Music, Spotify, and YouTube Music, the DOJ said. He then employed software that pushed the bots to continuously stream songs that he claimed to own, which the DOJ said were AI-generated.
By his arrest in 2024, he had created “hundreds of thousands of AI-generated songs,” then dispersed billions of automated streams among them so that the bots could avoid raising any red flags by all targeting the same song at once. All together, the fake songs generated substantially more streams than some of the most popular artists today, however. According to the DOJ, in a glaring example from April 2023, Smith’s fake songs were fraudulently streamed 80.9 million times during that month, while Taylor Swift’s entire catalog only got 9.3 million streams during the same time period.

Nous avons essayé la fonction avec deux véritables interviews en français : la qualité du texte est prometteuse, mais le traitement s’est montré long, fastidieux et parfois peu fiable.
ChatGPT accepte désormais officiellement les fichiers audio dans ses conversations. Réunions, interviews ou cours peuvent être transcrits, résumés ou transformés en notes structurées. Il est ensuite possible de poser des questions sur leur contenu comme on le ferait avec un document. La fonction est pour l'instant réservée aux abonnements ChatGPT payants et aux espaces de travail, Enterprise compris. L'offre gratuite n'y a pas accès. OpenAI prévient également que sa disponibilité peut varier selon la région, le modèle utilisé, la version de l'application et les réglages du workspace.
La transcription n'est toutefois pas nouvelle chez OpenAI. Whisper puis les modèles GPT-4o Transcribe permettaient déjà aux développeurs d'effectuer ce travail via l'API. Ce qui change ici est surtout l'usage : plus besoin d'API ni d'outil spécifique, il suffit théoriquement de déposer son fichier dans ChatGPT.

L’initiative, lancée par Advens for People and Planet, propose aux acteurs de l’économie sociale et solidaire des formations et un accompagnement gratuit pour les aider à renforcer leur cybersécurité et leur conformité au RGPD.

Après un bootcamp et de nombreux accompagnements pro bono, Cyber for Good ESS lance l’Academy, une série de webinaires consacrés à ces enjeux qui débute le 14 octobre 2026. L’objectif ? Donner à des structures souvent moins bien armées face aux cybermenaces les moyens d’adopter les bons réflexes et de mieux protéger leurs données.
Une heure par mois, de l’infrastructure à la gestion de crise

articles.title: OpenSSH 10.6 deliberately breaks two features in the name of security

OpenSSH 10.6 deliberately breaks two features in the name of security
OpenSSH 10.6, released Tuesday, makes compression less effective and rejects some usernames that previously worked, and the maintainers knew both changes would break things when they shipped them.
One change disables the LZ77 dictionary coder used for SSH compression after researchers found that sharing compression state across multiple channels could expose plaintext. The other blocks $ and \ in command-line usernames to prevent them from being interpreted by the shell through directives such as ProxyCommand and Match exec.
The release comes as OpenSSH sees more security research conducted with AI models, while those models get better at finding exploitable flaws. Other researchers later found some of those bugs independently. OpenSSH warned that adversaries who don’t report what they find “are likely to be able to discover these bugs too,” and for now, the project plans to release fixes more often rather than wait for its usual release schedule.

articles.title: Chemistry Nobel goes to reactions like those that gave life a hand
articles.summary:
Life is remarkably selective. Life relies on many molecules with what is termed “handedness”—they’re chemically identical but are mirror images of each other. Most chemical reactions will make a 50-50 mix of the left- and right-handed forms of a chemical, but life uses only one of them. In fact, because of the differences between left- and right-handed chemicals, most of the key enzymes used by organisms will fail to work if they’re presented with chemicals that have the wrong handedness.
That poses a bit of a challenge for origin-of-life research, as we’re forced to explain how a world that may have started with an even mix of left- and right-handed chemicals produced organisms that only used one of them.
Today’s Nobel Prize in Chemistry goes to two individuals, Henri Kagan and Kenso Soai, who discovered chemical reactions could be biased, producing large excesses of one of the two forms of a chemical.
Chirality and life
The technical term for molecular handedness is “chirality,” and scientists replace left and right with dextro (D) and levo (L). But the ideas are largely the same. Your hands have all the same components—fingers and thumbs—organized in the same way. Yet if you point your thumb upward, the fingers curl in opposite directions, making one the mirror image of the other. Depending on the arrangements of the chemical bonds, many molecules can form similar mirror-image forms, with all the same parts oriented slightly differently in space.

Redis by proxy: Percona targets the last major hurdle to Valkey adoption
When Redis changed its licensing in 2024, replacing its permissive BSD license with proprietary, source-available alternatives, it prompted a major split in the community. Within days, the Linux Foundation launched Valkey, an open source fork.
While Redis did subsequently change course again, adding the copyleft AGPLv3 open source license as an option in 2025, Valkey was already forging its own path for organizations that wanted a permissively licensed project with independent governance.
Much has happened in the intervening months, with Valkey moving to reduce its memory requirements, introducing new cluster management and access-control features, and more recently starting to use AI agents to help with maintenance work such as backporting fixes.

The big picture: OpenAI has published 722 papers generated by an internal AI model, reporting advances across hundreds of mathematical problems. The papers cover number theory, algebraic geometry, and other fields. The release comes amid objections from mathematicians who argue that using proprietary AI models to solve mathematical problems prioritizes results over understanding and leaves researchers unable to examine the systems behind the proofs.
OpenAI organized the results into 372 groups and said it had given the model about 4,000 problems. The release gives researchers a large collection of proofs to examine, but not access to the proprietary system that produced them.
The company reported advances related to three of the five remaining Millennium Prize Problems, including the Riemann hypothesis. That does not mean it has solved all three. Even so, the reported Riemann result prompted a strong response from Rutgers University distinguished mathematics professor Alex Kontorovich.
"If a human did this, it would be an instant Fields Medal, no questions asked," he wrote on X.
Alongside the papers, OpenAI released summaries of the model's "chain of thought" for 10 results. The summaries describe the model's reasoning on selected problems, though they cover only a small share of the published work.

L’association qualifie la Chine de « concurrent systémique ». Elle se dit pourtant favorable à un commerce ouvert, à condition que les règles déjà en place soient appliquées de façon cohérente.
D’après les données de marché du ZIV, la Chine est le premier fabricant mondial de vélos, avec 70 à 80 millions d’unités produites chaque année. L’Allemagne en sort environ 2 millions, soit 35 à 40 fois moins. Selon l’association, la pression sur le marché européen s’accentue : elle a d’abord touché les composants, puis de plus en plus les vélos complets, alors que la Chine s’est installée comme premier fournisseur de vélos électriques en Europe.
Le ZIV attribue cette évolution à la politique industrielle menée par Pékin sur le long terme. Proxy name in the agents’ web traffic pointed to Tencent’s Hunyuan models.
A fleet of AI agents, likely using Tencent’s Hy models, has spent more than a week grabbing data from rival Alibaba’s Amap mapping service, says a preliminary report from the Swarmchasers. The fleet, which ran its code on Tencent Cloud behind a hysandbox-ats proxy, reached a peak of 1,810 URL query scans on Oct. 4 alone. The Swarmchasers, a group of researchers, also noted 211 scans labeled “claude,” a reference to Anthropic’s AI models, though the code behind them matches Chinese models, not Claude.
The free urlquery.net service works by opening a web address in a sandboxed remote browser, with a public record of the scan. It’s used to verify suspicious and risky links and also helps agents reach pages they otherwise would not be able to touch directly. Leveraging the service for this type of agent work is not new, as the nonprofit lab Transluce tied some urlquery activity to OpenAI’s agents last month. The fleet in question this time used similar techniques, but on new targets and infrastructure.

articles.title: PA measles outbreak tops 1,000 cases, largest since disease was eliminated
articles.summary:
Pennsylvania’s explosive measles outbreak is now the largest the US has seen since the highly infectious virus was declared eliminated in 2000. With well over 1,000 cases, it’s the largest on record since 1991.
Pennsylvania’s health officials reported 1,078 measles cases in all of 2026 as of this afternoon. That includes 12 cases in January and March, with the remaining 1,066 cases since April, when the current outbreak began. The tally includes 145 cases recorded in the last seven days and 74 identified since the previous update on Monday. Health officials noted that 40 of the 74 cases added today were from more than two weeks ago and are just now being recorded.
Among the cases, there have been 207 hospitalizations and five deaths—a newborn, a 6-week-old, an 18-year-old, a 20-year-old, and a 40-year-old. All of the deaths occurred during the current outbreak in people who were unvaccinated; the two infants were too young to have been vaccinated.
With slipping vaccination rates nationwide, measles outbreaks and cases have come roaring back in the past few years. A large outbreak in Texas that spanned January–August 2025 ended with 762 cases, while an outbreak in South Carolina ended in April with 997 cases, the previous record holder. Pennsylvania exceeds that handily with its 1,066 outbreak-linked cases as of today. With 34 new infections reported since Monday, the outbreak does not appear to be close to ending.

articles.title: Veteran actor Nana Patekar dies at 75
articles.summary:
Veteran actor Nana Patekar dies at 75
From powerful performances and National Awards to philanthropy through NAAM Foundation, Nana Patekar’s career spanned cinema, social work, and a lasting legacy.
Veteran actor Nana Patekar, known for his powerful performances and versatility, died at his Goa residence in the early hours of Thursday. He was 75. Patekar is suspected to have suffered a heart attack, according to sources.

Im Mai 2025 hatte Google den SynthID Detector präsentiert, ein Tool, das per Google-KI erstellte Inhalte erkennen soll. Basis ist SynthID, das hauseigene Wasserzeichen-Tool des Konzerns. Mittlerweile sind weitere KI-Anbieter eingestiegen, etwa OpenAI, Nvidia und Kakao.
Bald auch für Apple Intelligence
Eine Unterstützung für Apple Intelligence soll „bald“ folgen, wie Google mitteilt. Damit wäre der KI-Detektor eines der ersten Erkennungstools, das Bilder von Apples KI-Features wie Image Playground identifizieren kann, wie Engadget schreibt.
Google hat den SynthID Detector jetzt für alle Nutzer:innen freigeschaltet, nachdem bisher nur ausgewählte Journalist:innen und Forscher:innen Zugriff erhalten hatten. Auf der entsprechenden Website können Nutzer:innen Bilder, Videos und Audiodateien hochladen, um sie auf das Vorhandensein einer SynthID hin untersuchen zu lassen.
Nur eigene Wasserzeichen erkannt
Ist der Inhalt von einem KI-Tool der oben genannten Anbieter erstellt worden – und ein Wasserzeichen vorhanden –, weist Google entsprechend daraufhin. Findet der SynthID Detector nichts, heißt das derweil nicht, dass es sich nicht um einen KI-generierten Inhalt handeln kann. Es bedeutet lediglich, dass kein Google-Wasserzeichen integriert ist.

Since its founding in 2004, it’s arguable that no network vendor has made better switches than Arista Networks Inc. That was true then and remains true, as its prowess in this area helped it ride the cloud boom and the artificial intelligence wave.
That model is changing as AI scales. Today, ahead of next week’s Open Compute Project Global Summit in San Jose, Arista announced an expansion of its AI network strategy from switches to rack scale.
Arista is launching an open Ethernet rack-scale portfolio covering both scale-up and scale-out AI fabrics, built with a large ecosystem of players such as Advanced Micro Devices Inc., Arm Ltd., Broadcom Inc., d-Matrix Corp., Meta Platforms Inc., Microsoft Corp. and Qualcomm Corp. The lead announcement is Etherlink SU-144, an Ethernet-based scale-up architecture that connects up to 144 accelerators, or XPUs, within a single-hop domain and up to 1,024 XPUs across racks. It is built on the Ethernet for Scale-Up Networking or ESUN initiative.
In the AI era, the network can no longer be thought of as an independent pipe moving data between servers. It has become a tightly integrated, rack-scale backplane, and how well it’s built determines how much value customers get from their compute. Les géants des télécoms français ont tendance à s'exporter à l'étranger ces dernières années. On connait ainsi les opérations d'Iliad (Free), très présent en Pologne, en Italie, et de plus en plus en Amérique latine. Et Orange n'est pas en reste de son côté. L'an dernier, le groupe français annonçait ainsi l'acquisition de l'Espagnol MasOrange, faisant d'Orange le numéro 1 du marché de ce pays. Et cette année, c'est du côté de l'Afrique que la société lorgne.
Orange veut racheter 70% de l'opérateur ghanéen Telecel Ghana
Orange va bien, comme nous le montrent les derniers résultats du groupe. Et cette bonne santé semble permettre des opérations de croissance externe intéressantes. Le média L'Informé nous indique ainsi qu'Orange a entamé des discussions pour s'avancer en Afrique anglophone, au Ghana plus précisément, pour acquérir l'opérateur Telecel Ghana.
L'objectif de la firme française serait d'acquérir au total 70% du capital de cet opérateur, ce qui en ferait l'actionnaire majoritaire. Orange pourrait boucler cette opération d'ici la fin de l'année, et lui permettrait de prendre pied dans un nouveau pays du continent africain, où le groupe n'était jusqu'alors pas présent.
L'Afrique, prochain moteur de croissance d'Orange ?

articles.title: El nuevo peligro de la IA: un agente puede engañar a otro para que robe información
articles.summary:
La expansión de los agentes de inteligencia artificial (IA) dentro de las empresas está abriendo una nueva puerta para los ciberdelincuentes. Investigaciones recientes muestran que un atacante puede manipular a uno de estos sistemas para que transmita instrucciones maliciosas a otros agentes de una misma organización y consiga acceso a información confidencial, bases de datos o recursos internos.
El problema fue identificado durante los últimos cinco meses en organizaciones como JPMorgan Chase, Rapid7, Weaviate y organismos gubernamentales de Francia. Aunque estas entidades no tienen una relación directa, todas utilizan agentes de IA conectados entre sí para ejecutar tareas de manera automática.
La técnica aprovecha una debilidad sencilla de explicar: un agente de IA puede confiar demasiado en otro agente. Si uno recibe una instrucción maliciosa y la transmite como si fuera una tarea legítima, el siguiente sistema puede ejecutarla sin comprobar suficientemente su origen.
Cómo funciona el ataque contra los agentes de IA
Para entender el riesgo, hay que imaginar una empresa en la que varios empleados especializados trabajan en cadena. Uno analiza documentos, otro consulta una base de datos y un tercero prepara un informe. Si uno de ellos recibe una orden falsa y los demás confían en él, el atacante puede aprovechar esa relación para avanzar dentro de la organización.

PM Modi calls for global framework to tackle cyber frauds, deepfakes, digital crimes
Inaugurating the tenth edition of the India Mobile Congress (IMC) 2026, Modi said governments, technology companies, telecom operators and financial institutions should create mechanisms to curb digital frauds.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday called for a global framework to tackle cyber frauds and deepfakes, saying digital threats have crossed national boundaries and require coordinated action by all stakeholders.
Inaugurating the tenth edition of the India Mobile Congress (IMC) 2026, Modi said governments, technology companies, telecom operators and financial institutions should create mechanisms to curb digital frauds.
"I urge the GSMA and telecom operators across the world: come, let us create a global mechanism that can stop such fraud before it reaches the people. India has learnt a lot from its experiences in this direction, and India is always ready to share its experiences with the world," Modi said.
Technology can achieve scale only when it gains people's trust, he said.
A person sitting in one country, with the help of a person in another country, can commit a crime in a third country, Modi said, adding that deepfakes have become a big challenge.

Someone "clicked on a link in an email"
- A successful phishing attack at the Arizona Supreme Court led to data compromise
- More than a million people are now thought to be affected
- The court's operations were not disrupted
The Arizona Supreme Court has suffered a cyberattack in which it lost sensitive data on more than a million people after an employee allegedly “clicked a malicious link in an email”, which led to the compromise of information on 1.3 million people.
Information is still scarce on the issue, as we don’t know if that malicious link resulted in the victim’s device being infected with an infostealer, or if they were asked to log into a bogus portal, allowing the threat actors to access their account directly.
It was confirmed that the threat actors copied information on 1.3 million people with unpaid court fees, fines and restitution payments for traffic and criminal violations dating back 30 years. Google libera detector de IA para qualquer pessoa
SynthID Detector verifica se arquivos contêm marcas d'água de IA. A novidade analisa imagens, vídeos e áudios.
O Google acaba de liberar mais um recurso de inteligência artificial. Desta vez, não é algo para produzir conteúdo, mas para detectá-lo: a companhia anunciou o SynthID Detector para permitir que qualquer pessoa analise uma imagem, um vídeo ou um áudio para descobrir se esse arquivo foi gerado por IA.
Esta não é uma ferramenta exatamente nova. O próprio Google explica que o SynthID Detector foi introduzido no ano passado, em fase de prévia, “para ajudar profissionais de mídia a verificar conteúdo gerado por IA”.
Agora, depois de ter sido aperfeiçoado, o SynthID Detector está sendo liberado para qualquer pessoa, em escala global. O seu uso é fácil: acesse o site do serviço, toque ou clique no campo principal e faça upload de um arquivo de mídia para ser analisado.
Em seguida, a ferramenta informará se aquele conteúdo foi gerado ou editado com inteligência artificial. Ou quase isso (você já vai entender).
Podemos imaginar que o SynthID Detector simplesmente analisa um arquivo para encontrar características que sugerem que aquela mídia tem traços de IA. Mas não é bem assim: o que a ferramenta faz, na verdade, é verificar se o arquivo tem uma marca d’água digital inserida por um mecanismo de IA compatível.

articles.title: La factura de la luz del usuario medio supera los 104 euros pese al récord de generación solar en España
articles.summary:
La energía solar fotovoltaica lideró el mix eléctrico durante el mes de septiembre por sexto mes consecutivo. Y, sin embargo, la que es la tecnología más barata no ha conseguido evitar por sí sola el impacto que ha tenido la inflación en los precios de la energía en la tarifa regulada (PVPC), a la que están acogidos 8,2 millones de consumidores, un 27,4% del total.
Según un estudio de FACUA-Consumidores en Acción, la factura eléctrica del usuario medio de esta modalidad ha subido casi 40 euros en apenas cinco meses, hasta superar los 104 euros en septiembre. Se trata del recibo más caro de los últimos cuatro años.
Lo que dice el informe. La factura del usuario medio acogido al PVPC en septiembre ha subido un 28% con respecto al mismo mes de 2025 (que registró un precio de 57,85 euros) y un 7,9% con respecto a agosto (con 96,65 euros), prolongando una tendencia alcista que comenzó en mayo. Esto significa que el mes pasado, el recibo del usuario medio con PVPC alcanzó los 104,31 euros, una cifra que no se superaba desde 2022, cuando el impacto de la crisis energética provocada por la invasión rusa de Ucrania llevó el recibo hasta los 137,93 euros.
Para realizar sus cálculos, FACUA utiliza el perfil de un usuario medio con una potencia contratada de 4,4 kW (la misma en horario punta y valle) y un consumo de 366 kWh mensuales.

For those unfamiliar, hybrid bonding creates a permanent bond between two silicon chips using embedded metal bumps that are fused together to form a single chip. articles.title: OpenAI publishes 722 AI-generated math discoveries in major scientific milestone - SiliconANGLE
articles.summary:
OpenAI publishes 722 AI-generated math discoveries in major scientific milestone
OpenAI Group PBC has published 722 math papers that it generated using an unreleased artificial intelligence model.
Some of the papers, which were posted to GitHub late Tuesday, prove long-running hypotheses. Others disapprove proposed explanations of mathematical phenomena or narrow down the possible answers to complex, yet-unsolved puzzles. Overall, OpenAI’s papers span about 20 mathematical subfields.
One of the most notable discoveries relates to the Riemann hypothesis. It’s a more than 150-year-old paper about prime numbers, numbers that can only be divided by themselves or one. The Riemann hypothesis argues that prime numbers follow a pattern described by a mathematical object called the Riemann zeta function.
Proving the conjecture is considered to be one of the most important challenges in mathematics. Its significance partly stems from the fact that many later math papers are based on the assumption the Riemann hypothesis is correct. In other words, proving the Riemann hypothesis would verify those papers.
OpenAI’s unreleased AI model didn’t manage to come up with a complete answer. However, it did prove an important piece of the puzzle called the quasi-Riemann hypothesis.
Theoretical computer science was another major focus of OpenAI’s research exercise. The company’s unreleased AI model produced more than 80 papers about the topic.

articles.title: US government, tech giants and Biohub commit $1.8B to AI biology initiative - SiliconANGLE
articles.summary:
US government, tech giants and Biohub commit $1.8B to AI biology initiative
More than a half-dozen public and private sector organizations are teaming up to develop biology datasets for artificial intelligence models.
The consortium, which announced the collaboration today, is committing $1.8 billion to the project.
Studying how a cell responds to a new therapy usually requires scientists to set up a physical test environment. That can take years of work and millions of dollars. A faster, more cost-efficient approach would be to test therapies using simulated cells. A simulation doesn’t require expensive lab equipment and can theoretically be spun up in a few hours.
Ultra-detailed, highly reliable simulations that can substitute lab equipment aren’t yet available. The reason is that creating such virtual cells would require a new generation of biology-optimized AI models. Training such models would only be possible with bigger biology datasets than those presently available to scientists.
The research initiative announced today aims to produce the necessary datasets. The biggest contributor to the project is the U.S. Department of Energy, which will commit more than $500 million over five years.
Some of the funds are earmarked for microscopy equipment. The hardware will be used to collect cell measurements for AI training datasets.

Shawn Fanning, programador y estudiante de la Northeastern University de Boston, entra en el canal de IRC "w00w00" para charlar con "Man0War", "Mars" y "Nocarrier", amigos online a los que jamás había visto en persona. No solo quería hablar: buscaba ideas para una comunidad online, una que se expandiría por Internet como la pólvora y pondría en jaque a toda una industria. Fue una conversación interesante que dio paso a meses de trabajo intenso hasta que, en junio de 1999, Fanning subió la primera versión de Napster a Internet.
Han pasado más de 27 años desde que Napster viera la luz y crease la primera gran red P2P de intercambio de música. En un momento en el que enviar un archivo podía llevar minutos, si no horas, Fanning había creado un servicio fácil, accesible y, sobre todo, rápido, gracias al formato MP3. El pico de uso verificado llegó en febrero de 2001, con 26,4 millones de usuarios, aunque algunas estimaciones hablan de hasta 80 millones de cuentas registradas que compartían sus archivos con otros a cambio de que estos hiciesen lo mismo. Esta es su historia.
Tras años de amistad online, Sean Parker ("man0war") y Shawn Fanning ("napster") se reunieron por primera vez para darle forma a Napster. Eso es precisamente lo que empieza a ocurrir con Windows 10. Casi un año después de que terminara su soporte ordinario, quienes han decidido prolongar su vida útil entran ahora en una fase en la que quedarse empieza a resultar bastante más caro.
Windows 10 ya vive una prórroga. Microsoft puso fin al soporte estándar del sistema el 14 de octubre de 2025, pero eso no significó que todos los equipos tuvieran que dejar de utilizarlo de un día para otro. Para quienes necesitaban más tiempo abrió Extended Security Updates, o ESU, un programa que permite continuar recibiendo determinadas actualizaciones de seguridad después de esa fecha.
El precio se duplica. Durante el primer año de ESU, la tarifa comercial base ha sido de 61 dólares por cada dispositivo con Windows 10 incluido en el programa. Cuando comience el segundo año, pasará a 122 dólares, y Microsoft ya había establecido que volverá a duplicarse hasta los 244 dólares en el tercero y último. Hay además un detalle importante: las licencias son acumulativas. Si una organización se incorpora directamente en el segundo año, no puede adquirir únicamente ese periodo, sino que debe cubrir también el primero.

articles.title: El Himalaya se está llenando de tantísimos turistas que ya hay pájaros cambiando su forma de cantar
articles.summary:
En el Himalaya hay faisanes que están cambiando radicalmente su forma de cantar. Y hay un sospechoso claro que explica esa transformación: el turismo masivo. A medida que la cordillera se convierte en un destino de aventura soñado por viajeros de todo el mundo, los monales (Lophophorus impejanus) están alterando su forma de comunicarse. En las zonas masificadas, las aves alcanzan frecuencias más altas cuando cantan. También emiten llamadas más breves que sus compañeras de los valles menos concurridos por turistas.
Para los científicos ese cambio tiene poco de misterioso: con él los monales intentan hacerse oír por encima del ruido de los humanos que (cada vez más) ocupan su hábitat.
¿Qué ha pasado? Que un grupo de investigadores indios se ha llevado un par de sorpresas mientras estudiaba poblaciones de monal, un faisán originario de los bosques montañosos del Himalaya que ha sido elevado a la categoría de símbolo patrio tanto en el estado indio de Uttarakhand como en Nepal.
El problema es que ninguna de esas 'sorpresas' es buena. Lo que han constatado el doctor Rajeev Lochan y sus colegas de la Universidad Hemvati Nandan Bahuguna Garhwal es que los humanos estamos alterando el entorno de la especie hasta tal punto que ha empezado a variar algunos de sus hábitos. Sus conclusiones las han plasmado en dos papers científicos.
¿Qué cambios han percibido? Probablemente el más interesante es el que afecta a la forma de comunicarse de los faisanes del Himalaya. Durante más o menos un…

MENA startup funding surges to $1.1 billion in September 2026
MENA startup funding staged a sharp comeback in September, crossing the $1 billion mark for the first time in months as a string of large Saudi fintech deals pulled the region out of August’s slowdown.
Startups across the Middle East and North Africa raised $1.1 billion through 73 deals during the month, up 193% from August. Yet the recovery looks less dramatic when compared with last year: funding remained 68% below September 2025.
The rebound was also highly concentrated.
Barq’s $329.5 million Series A, Tabby’s $233 million Series F and Lendo’s $200 million debt financing together brought in $762.5 million, accounting for nearly 70% of all capital raised during the month.
That concentration offers a more nuanced picture of September. Capital returned in force, but it flowed disproportionately to a handful of large, predominantly Saudi fintech companies rather than evenly across the ecosystem.
Debt also remained a significant feature of the funding landscape, accounting for 31.7% of September’s total. That is substantially lower than the 76% recorded in September 2025, suggesting equity played a much larger role in this year’s headline figure.
Saudi Arabia takes back the lead
Saudi Arabia returned to the top of the regional funding table in September, with 40 startups raising a combined $947.2 million.

articles.summary:
Seagate and Toshiba battle for TDK's HDD head business, a critical hard drive component — multi-billion-dollar deal threatens sole independent supplier as shortages intensify
What if Toshiba loses the bid?
Seagate Technology and Toshiba are reportedly competing to acquire TDK's hard disk drive magnetic head business in a transaction valued at several billion dollars, reports Bloomberg. For Seagate, the acquisition would expand the supply of HDD heads that it also produces internally, but for Toshiba, TDK is the only way for it to get magnetic heads for its hard drives. If Seagate buys TDK's HDD heads operation, then Toshiba's HDD business will depend on supply from Seagate.
TDK is the world's only independent supplier of HDD magnetic heads and Toshiba's sole source of the components. By contrast, Seagate and Western Digital manufacture heads internally and also buy them from TDK if they need to. In recent years, TDK started to produce HDD heads for Seagate's drives that rely on heat-assisted magnetic recording (HAMR) technology, Western Digital's products featuring energy-assisted magnetic recording (EAMR), and Toshiba's HDDs based on microwave-assisted magnetic recording (MAMR) technology, which makes it an important supplier for all hard drive manufacturers.
Yet, while Seagate and Western Digital produce magnetic heads internally, they also source them from TDK when they need additional supply to respond to increases in demand. Toshiba, by contrast, depends entirely on TDK …

Google trabaja en una función que busca resolver el principal punto débil del desbloqueo facial en los Pixel: la poca luz. Se trata de Face Active Illumination, detectada en el código de la beta 1 de Android 17 QPR3, según Android Authority.
La función aparece dentro de los ajustes de Face Unlock y, aunque todavía está en una fase temprana de desarrollo, apunta a ser la respuesta definitiva de Android a Face ID, el sistema de reconocimiento facial que Apple lanzó hace casi una década.
Cómo funciona Face Active Illumination de Android
El código de la beta incluye un interruptor general para activar o desactivar la función, además de una escala de brillo con tres niveles ajustables mediante un control deslizante.

Le passage en caisse pourrait devenir nettement moins confortable pour des millions de salariés. Alors que l’Assemblée nationale examine une réforme des titres-restaurant, plusieurs amendements, notamment portés par des élus MoDem et Renaissance, proposaient de limiter leur utilisation dans les magasins, tout en conservant un plafond de 25 euros au restaurant.

Une proposition MoDem fixant cette limite à 15 euros hors restaurants a été rejetée. Le texte doit être débattu dans l’hémicycle le 12 octobre, où ces pistes pourraient être proposées à nouveau.
À la caisse, 15 euros à sortir autrement ?
Sur un panier de 25 euros composé uniquement de produits éligibles, un salarié peut actuellement tout régler avec ses titres s’il dispose du solde nécessaire. Avec un plafond ramené à 10 euros, il devrait payer les 15 euros restants avec sa carte bancaire ou un autre moyen de paiement.

Los vecinos de Belicena, una localidad perteneciente a Vegas del Genil, en Granada, llevan alrededor de una semana preocupados por la aparición de algo tan bonito como peligroso en sus calles. Se trata del estramonio (Datura stramonium), una planta muy tóxica, conocida por su contenido en alcaloides como la atropina o la escopolamina (coloquialmente llamada burundanga). Todo comenzó cuando el Ayuntamiento cambió la tierra de algunos de los arriates de la urbanización del Ventorrillo. Por eso, lo primero que han hecho desde la Plataforma Vecinal Defiende Vegas del Genil ha sido ponerse en contacto con el consistorio.
De momento, según ha explicado a Xataka su presidente, Francisco José Luque Navarro, no han recibido una respuesta. También han hablado con expertos, pero han obtenido consejos heterogéneos. Unos dicen que no hay peligro siempre que no se coma. Otros, que deben extremar las precauciones. ¿A quién deberían hacer caso entonces?
Una planta común, pero peligrosa
Según explican desde el Ministerio de Transición Ecológica y Reto Demográfico (MITECO), el estramonio es una planta naturalizada en casi todas las zonas templadas y cálidas del mundo. Puede encontrarse naturalmente en cultivos como el girasol, el maíz, el olivo o la remolacha, y también en zonas urbanas. Se reproduce muy eficazmente a través de semillas capaces de germinar en cualquier momento del año si las condiciones son favorables. articles.title: Ahorra más de 20 dólares en vacaciones: solo debes desconectar estos electrodomésticos
articles.summary:
Salir de casa durante varios días permite reducir el consumo eléctrico, incluso sin contar el ahorro por no utilizar la cocina, la lavadora o el lavavajillas.
La Organización de Consumidores y Usuarios de España (OCU) calcula que desconectar electrodomésticos e instalaciones antes de unas vacaciones puede reducir la factura hasta en 20 dólares.
Además, dejar determinados aparatos apagados y preparar las instalaciones disminuye el riesgo de averías, incendios, pérdidas de agua y problemas de seguridad durante la ausencia.
Cuánto dinero consume un refrigerador
El refrigerador es uno de los aparatos que más energía demanda cuando funciona de forma continua. La OCU estima que mantener un modelo combi encendido durante un mes puede costar cerca de 3,5 dólares, mientras que una nevera grande de tipo americano puede alcanzar los 7 dólares mensuales.
Si la ausencia será prolongada, la pauta de expertos es vaciarlo, desconectarlo, limpiarlo y dejar la puerta entreabierta. Esa última medida ayuda a evitar olores y la aparición de moho.

Giant artificial intelligence rounds have pushed U.S. venture capital deal value about 44% past its previous annual record with a quarter still to go, according to the quarterly PitchBook-NVCA Venture Monitor report released today, but the exits needed to return that money to investors have not kept pace.
Much of the $515.8 billion invested in the first nine months of the year went to OpenAI Group PBC and Anthropic PBC, which between them raised more than $200 billion in the first half. Without those rounds, PitchBook’s analysts said, the dollar totals have held to much the same trend since late 2024.
Third-quarter deal value fell about 40%, to $98.4 billion, and most of the drop came out of venture-growth rounds. Startups kept closing deals at a near-record pace regardless. PitchBook counts an estimated 5,012 in the quarter, and its records show only one busier quarter, at the start of 2022.
AI accounts for a record 82.7% of the year’s deal value, although its share of each quarter has been shrinking since January and fell to 65.9% in the third. Databricks Inc. took the quarter’s largest check at $5 billion. That was “a far cry” from the triple-digit billions frontier labs raised earlier in the year, the report said.

Pavel Rabtsevich, chercheur indépendant installé à Tarragone, en Espagne, épluchait les archives publiques du télescope spatial TESS de la NASA avec Claude Code, l'agent de programmation d'Anthropic, quand une étoile s'est mise à clignoter bizarrement. Son récit, publié sur Reddit, s'adosse à un preprint déposé le 25 septembre 2026 sur Zenodo, l'entrepôt scientifique hébergé par le CERN. L'auteur s'en tient scrupuleusement au terme de planète candidate.
TIC 4206066, une possible super-Terre de 1,4 rayon terrestre
L'astre, une naine de type K cataloguée TIC 4206066 et située selon lui à 116 années-lumière, perd environ 0,05 % de son éclat pendant deux heures, tous les 3,18 jours. Le motif surgit dans des relevés de fin 2025, puis dans ceux de 2020 et de 2018 : 23 transits au total. Si l'objet tourne bien autour de cette étoile, son rayon atteint 1,4 fois celui de la Terre. Un second signal, nettement plus fragile, évoque un corps de 2,2 rayons terrestres bouclant son orbite en 11,13 jours.
Le preprint chiffre la probabilité de faux positif entre 3 et 4 % et précise qu'aucune validation statistique n'est revendiquée.
	
Retrouver un signal dans le secteur 110 ne prouverait pas qu'il s'agit d'une planète, et un résultat indécis ne montrerait pas que ce n'en est pas une.

“Tata is for TOLL, and Suchi is for TO-252 packaging,” Makoto Terada, managing director of Rohm Semiconductor India, told EE Times. TOLL is widely used in the two-wheeler market, while Terada said the main customer base for TO-252 is “more like four-wheeler.”
The move is part of a broader change in Rohm’s manufacturing strategy. The company has historically manufactured most of its chips in its own fabs, but has increased its use of external manufacturing partners in recent years. It is evaluating the two partnerships to prototype and benchmark the capabilities of the Indian OSATs, with the aim of starting production for the local market before potentially expanding production to serve global demand.
“There are so many OSAT companies and partners, but at this moment, today, we do not know yet who will be the best,” Terada said.
The company started with two partners to move faster. Asked whether both partners could eventually handle the same packages, Terada said, “That is possible,” but added that it would depend on demand.

articles.title: Qué es intranet, para qué sirve y cómo se ha usado en gobiernos, universidades y escuelas
articles.summary:
Las organizaciones recurren cada vez más a redes privadas de comunicación interna para ordenar su funcionamiento diario. Una intranet permite a empleados, docentes, estudiantes o funcionarios acceder a información, gestionar trámites y colaborar entre sí dentro de un entorno cerrado y protegido, distinto de internet.
Esta herramienta se ha extendido tanto en el sector privado como en instituciones públicas, universidades y escuelas, donde cumple funciones específicas según las necesidades de cada comunidad.
A diferencia de una red abierta, la intranet exige autenticación mediante credenciales y aplica medidas de seguridad adicionales para proteger datos sensibles. Funciona mediante la interconexión de computadoras, servidores y otros dispositivos, y utiliza protocolos similares a los de internet, como HTTP y HTTPS, pero restringidos al uso interno.
Qué es una intranet y cuál es su función principal
Una intranet es una red privada pensada para uso exclusivo dentro de una organización, con el objetivo de agilizar la comunicación, centralizar la información y facilitar la colaboración entre sus integrantes. articles.title: New Linux tech compresses memory in RAM, as RAM, for 452x speedup — new CRAM method offers giant boost to compressed memory reads
articles.summary:
New Linux tech compresses memory in RAM, as RAM, for 452x speedup — new CRAM method offers giant boost to compressed memory reads
The new method allows access using standard memory semantics instead of as a block device, drastically improving performance.
A new compression model, called CRAM, offers a different path to compression that avoids swap entirely by keeping the compressed data in memory, and it offers up to 452x the performance of ZRAM. I was a kid in the 1990s when the idea seemed so simple to me: I can use PKZIP to compress my files, so why can't we do that with RAM? Indeed, I am not a singular genius, and many other people had the same idea, so memory compression has been a feature of most operating systems for a long time. In Linux, the most popular options are zswap and ZRAM, but both of these options are fundamentally swap-layer features. CRAM is a new take that claims to boost performance tremendously.
CRAM was conceptualized by Gregory Price and his team at Meta. The central realization that seems to have spurred the development of CRAM is that the largest portion of the performance hit from compressed memory isn't the compression; that's tiny. No, the largest hit apparently stems mostly from the fault itself and the swap behavior. So the thinking seems to have been "what if we just do zram, but completely in memory instead of as swap?"

articles.title: Fake ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude Ad Portals Capture Credentials and MFA Codes
articles.summary:
Cybersecurity researchers have disclosed details of a "human-operated phishing platform" that impersonates advertising products for artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots like Google Gemini, Anthropic Claude, OpenAI ChatGPT, Perplexity, Meta Muse, and Manus.
The products, which claim to offer campaign optimization, spend audits, and business-account connections, are designed with one goal in mind: to capture credentials and multi-factor authentication (MFA) codes via spoofed login windows using the browser-in-the-browser (BitB) trick.
"Each product was built around the same action: Connect," Island researchers Oleg Zaytsev and Ofek Ronen said in a report shared with The Hacker News. "Clicking it opened a browser drawn inside the real browser. The fake address bar displayed trusted origins such as accounts.google.com or an Okta tenant, while the real browser remained on the phishing domain."
"Behind the interface, the platform kept every password attempt, fingerprinted the device, and let an operator pick which MFA challenge the victim saw next."

Sin duda, se trata de un avance que podría mejorar significativamente la sostenibilidad de estas instalaciones, cuestionadas por su elevado consumo de recursos.
El dispositivo, de seis metros de altura y recubierto en metal, funciona con materiales llamados MOF (estructuras organometálicas), una especie de esponja molecular capaz de atrapar moléculas de agua incluso en aire muy seco. El espacio interior de un gramo de MOF podría cubrir dos canchas de fútbol, explicó Yaghi. Esas estructuras pueden almacenar hidrógeno para generar energía limpia, dióxido de carbono para purificar el aire o, como en este caso, agua.
Cómo saca agua del aire sin electricidad
El aire pasa a través del MOF, que atrae las moléculas de agua y las retiene en sus poros. El material permanece seco al tacto aun saturado y no libera una sola gota al exprimirlo: solo el calor logra liberar el agua retenida. El prototipo que Atoco mostró en su planta de Irvine, California, puede funcionar con humedad relativa de apenas el 13% y libera agua con calor de hasta 38 grados centígrados.

"When visiting such a site, users were shown a forged Cloudflare verification page that, under the pretext of confirming the visitor is human, prompted them to execute a command," CERT-UA said in an advisory. "Executing the command caused a malicious MSI package to be downloaded and installed from a remote server (the ClickFix technique)."
The attacks also make use of the EtherHiding technique to retrieve the domain name of the resource from which the fake verification page is loaded, as well as the script's operating mode, from a smart contract on the Polygon or Ethereum network.
According to CERT-UA, there are three operating modes: 0 – inactive; 1 – passive tracking of visitors that includes gathering data about the website and the page from which the visitor arrived; and 2 – displaying the fake verification page.

The catch: nobody can check it against their clocks yet
- Singapore's CQT reports two lutetium-ion clocks with record-evaluated uncertainties of 1.2 and 1.3 × 10⁻¹⁹, making them the most accurate atomic clocks to date
- The stated results top Wuhan's calcium clock (4.4 × 10⁻¹⁹) and NIST's aluminum clock (5.5 × 10⁻¹⁹) by a wide berth
- It lands days before the CGPM meets in Versailles, where a draft resolution admits no consensus on replacing cesium just yet
A team at the National University of Singapore (NUS) has put a single charged atom of lutetium at the top of the rankings for the world's most accurate clock.
The remarkable achievement was documented in a paper published in Nature, as researchers at NUS's Centre for Quantum Technologies (CQT) reported two lutetium-ion clocks with evaluated fractional uncertainties of 1.2 × 10⁻¹⁹ and 1.3 × 10⁻¹⁹, the lowest yet reported for any atomic clock.
"I am confident that what we have now is the most accurate clock in the world," team leader Murray Barrett said in the NUS announcement.
A significant leap in accuracy and why it matters
Computing the numbers, 1.2 × 10⁻¹⁹ corresponds to one second of error in roughly 264 billion years, consistent with reports that it would take more than 260 billion years to lose a second in accuracy.

articles.title: What Is Agentic Pentesting? What It Proves, and Where It Stops.
articles.summary:
If you’re evaluating an agentic pentesting solution right now, you’ve probably heard the same pitch more than once: point it at a target, and it discovers, validates, and exploits attack paths autonomously, the way a real attacker would.
That promise is worth taking seriously. It’s also worth pressure testing, and three questions do the heavy lifting.
- What can the assessment actually prove?
- When is that proof produced? And,
- How much of your environment does the proof cover?
Most evaluations stop at the first step. However, it’s at the second and third ones where validation programs are won or lost.
One note on where we stand: Picus builds and sells autonomous pentesting. That is exactly why we can be precise about where it ends, because the limits belong to the method, not to any vendor's implementation, and no roadmap can remove them.
The problem in four numbers
Four numbers from this year explain why the second and third questions now carry more weight than the first.
- Volume: 35,364 CVEs found in the first half of 2026, up 49.5% year over year.
- Prioritization: only 95 of roughly 39,600 CVEs published through August saw confirmed in-the-wild exploitation, so severity-led prioritization is effectively chasing the wrong list.
- Speed: mean time from disclosure to exploitation collapsed from 21.5 days in 2025 to 8 hours in 2026.
- Capacity: of the more than 26,000 vulnerabilities surfaced by AI-scale discovery, only 421 were patched upstream.

articles.summary:
La justicia de Estados Unidos condenó a Michael Smith, de 54 años, a 18 meses de prisión por un fraude de streaming musical basado en inteligencia artificial que le permitió cobrar más de ocho millones de dólares en regalías falsas. El hombre se había declarado culpable ante la corte.
Según un comunicado del Departamento de Justicia, Smith es la primera persona en el país acusada penalmente por fraude de streaming asistido por inteligencia artificial. El esquema funcionó sin ser detectado durante siete años, desde 2017 hasta su primera imputación en 2024. El tribunal también le ordenó devolver 8.091.843,64 dólares, el monto exacto que la fiscalía determinó que obtuvo con la maniobra.
Cómo funcionaba el fraude
Smith creó hasta 10.000 cuentas de bots en Amazon Music, Apple Music, Spotify y YouTube Music con correos electrónicos truchos y tarjetas de débito obtenidas de forma fraudulenta, informó el Departamento de Justicia. Luego usó un software para que esas cuentas reprodujeran sin parar canciones que él mismo decía haber compuesto.
Para el momento de su arresto, había generado cientos de miles de canciones con inteligencia artificial. Repartió miles de millones de reproducciones automáticas entre ellas para que los bots no concentraran la actividad en un solo tema y evitaran así alertar a las plataformas.

FortiBleed was first documented by SOCRadar and Hudson Rock in June 2026, with the activity targeting thousands of Fortinet firewalls as part of a global campaign. For years, the enterprise cybersecurity story has been told as a straight line of escalation: more attacks, more data loss, more pressure, and more urgency. That narrative is still familiar, but comparing the five most recent years of Voice of the CISO research suggests a more useful reading. The CISO role has not simply become harder because every metric is rising at once. It has become harder because the center of risk has shifted and moved closer to the way work now gets done.
The latest 2026 findings show signs of progress. Fewer CISOs expect a material cyberattack in the next 12 months, and fewer report material loss of sensitive information than in 2025. articles.title: Do you need a mouse with an 8K polling rate?
articles.summary:
Do you need a mouse with an 8K polling rate?
Hint: You don't.
For years, the standard polling rate for gaming peripherals — mice, keyboards, etc. — has been 1,000 Hz, which equates to a delay, or latency, of 1 millisecond. This is significantly higher than the standard polling rate for non-gaming peripherals, by the way, which is 125 Hz (8ms latency) — in fact, it's eight times as fast.
Well, over the last couple of years, gaming companies have been asking: What if we made the polling rate even faster than 1,000 Hz? What if we made it eight times as fast?
And now just about every single ultra-lightweight, esports-oriented gaming mouse that comes out has up to an 8,000 Hz polling rate. And, of course, this raises the question every time: Do you actually need a mouse with an 8,000 Hz polling rate?
And the answer is... probably not.
What is polling rate, and what does it mean?
Polling rate is, simply put, how often your mouse communicates with your PC. That is, how often it reports mouse movement and clicks to your CPU. At a standard gaming mouse polling rate of 1,000 Hz, your mouse is communicating with your PC 1,000 times per second — or, once every millisecond. Hence, a 1,000 Hz polling rate means 1ms latency. At a standard non-gaming mouse polling rate of 125 Hz, your mouse is only communicating with your PC once every eight milliseconds — or an 8 ms latency. articles.title: Unpatched Critical LMCache Flaw Lets Unauthenticated Attackers Run Code Remotely
articles.summary:
A critical vulnerability in LMCache, open-source software that speeds up large language model (LLM) servers such as vLLM, lets an attacker run code on the cache server without logging in, and no fixed version is available.
The flaw is in LMCache's multiprocess mode, where the cache runs as a standalone server that LLM workers reach over the ZeroMQ messaging library. A single network message to that server can run commands as the user the LMCache process runs as.
The server can be reached from another machine only when an operator sets it to listen on a routable address, rather than the localhost it uses by default.
JFrog disclosed the flaw on October 7 and assigned it a severity score of 9.8 out of 10, in the critical range, the rating it gives a server bound to a routable address.
The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-105192, affects LMCache from version 0.3.9, released in October 2025, through 0.5.5, the latest stable release, and is also present in the 0.5.6 release candidates and the development branch. No fixed version exists.
Whether a server is exposed comes down to one setting. By default, the multiprocess server listens only on the local machine, so another host cannot reach it. It becomes reachable when an operator starts it with a routable address, much like multi-node deployments share a cache across machines.

articles.title: Attackers Hijack .gh, .sl, and .as Registries to Obtain Certificates for Google Domains
articles.summary:
Attackers compromised three country-code top-level domains (ccTLDs) and obtained unauthorized HTTPS certificates for several Google domains, Google said on October 6.
Google's own systems were not breached, but any domain ending in .gh (Ghana), .sl (Sierra Leone) or .as (American Samoa) was put at risk. With such a certificate, an attacker could pose as the real site over an encrypted connection and read the private data sent to it.
Chrome blocked the unauthorized certificates for Google's domains through CRLSets, its way of quickly blocking certificates in emergencies, Google said. The company also worked with the certificate authorities (CAs) that issued the certificates to have them revoked, a step meant to protect people using other browsers and apps.
Google did not name the domains. Certificate Transparency (CT) logs are the public record of certificates issued by CAs. They show at least 12 certificates issued between September 22 and 27 for Google and YouTube names under the three ccTLDs, including google.com.gh, google.sl and google.as.
A CA issues a certificate once the applicant shows control of the domain, for example by adding a record to the domain's DNS. The attackers changed authoritative DNS records during the hijacks, and Google has no reason to believe the CAs did anything wrong, the company said.

articles.title: Tensorlake npm Package Compromised to Deliver Shai-Hulud Credential-Stealing Worm
articles.summary:
The npm package known as "tensorlake," a TypeScript software development kit (SDK) for Tensorlake applications, sandboxes, and cloud services, was compromised as part of a ChainDrop / Shai-Hulud supply chain attack.
The malicious version 0.5.144 "contains obfuscated malware that harvests credentials, exfiltrates secrets, establishes persistence, and executes remotely supplied code," Socket said. Version 0.5.144 is no longer available for download from the npm package registry.
An analysis of the compromised release shows that it contains a preinstall hook designed to launch a JavaScript file ("package/lib/setup.mjs"), an obfuscated loader that launches the main credential-stealing and self-propagating worm ("package/lib/Math_Symbol.js") using the Bun runtime.
The stealer malware is designed to harvest credentials across local files, CI environments, Kubernetes, and Vault sources. It also drops the HackBrowserData binary, exfiltrates the collected data, establishes persistence on the host, and facilitates the execution of remotely-supplied code.
"That combination extends the risk beyond a single stolen API key," Socket said. "Any secrets accessible to the executing process may be exposed, and persistence can retain attacker access after the affected dependency is removed."

On s’est habitués à avoir des smartphones toujours plus grands. L’iPhone Duo propose une autre approche : sur son écran extérieur, Apple place le dock et les commandes principales sur la droite, et donc beaucoup plus près du pouce.

C’est probablement l’un des aspects les plus intéressants du format imaginé par Apple. Lorsque l’iPhone Duo est fermé, son écran extérieur ne reprend pas simplement iOS tel qu’on le connaît sur un iPhone classique. L’interface a été adaptée à la forme particulière de l’appareil, avec une zone d’affichage suffisamment large à gauche et les principaux éléments de navigation regroupés sur la droite.
On garde ainsi un écran assez grand pour consulter ses contenus, sans devoir contorsionner son doigt pour atteindre les commandes. articles.title: Les hackers IA de YesWeHack ont débusqué des failles chez Sanofi en quelques heures
articles.summary:
Sanofi a testé le pentest agentique avec YesWeHack, en laissant des agents d'IA attaquer cinq de ses applications web. Présenté aux Assises de la cybersécurité, le bilan est encourageant, même si l'IA ne remplace pas encore les hackers humains.
Confier à une intelligence artificielle le soin de pirater ses propres sites pour en repérer les faiblesses, c'est le principe du pentest agentique, que Sanofi a testé avec YesWeHack et présenté le mercredi 7 octobre aux Assises de la cybersécurité de Monaco, devant Clubic. En quelques heures, les agents d'IA ont déniché des failles que les outils automatiques classiques laissent d'habitude filer, comme un code de sécurité qu'on pouvait contourner au moment d'enregistrer une carte bancaire. Mais plus de la moitié de leurs trouvailles avaient déjà été signalées par des hackers humains, et la facture peut vite grimper. Le retour d'expérience dessine un outil utile, mais pas encore miraculeux.
Le pentest agentique, ou l'art de se cambrioler soi-même
Le test d'intrusion, ou pentest, est un vrai classique de la cybersécurité. Une entreprise paie des experts pour attaquer ses systèmes avant que de vrais pirates ne s'en chargent, puis reçoit un rapport qui détaille les failles trouvées. Sa version agentique conserve ce principe, tout en confiant l'attaque à des agents d'IA, des programmes capables d'enchaîner seuls les étapes d'un piratage. articles.title: Tesla met la pression sur les régulateurs européens pour faire homologuer son FSD
articles.summary:
Pour obtenir le feu vert de Bruxelles, Tesla a pesé sur l'évaluation du régulateur néerlandais et appelé ses clients à interpeller les ministres. Sept chercheurs en sécurité routière ont examiné les études transmises par le constructeur aux autorités européennes, et aucun n'a trouvé la preuve que le FSD sauve des vies.
Le vote des Vingt-Sept sur le Full Self-Driving (Supervised) de Tesla n'aura pas lieu avant décembre. Ce lundi le comité technique chargé des véhicules à moteur n'a consacré que 25 minutes de discussion au dossier. Le constructeur devra patienter au moins deux mois de plus. Pour décrocher une autorisation européenne, Tesla a besoin du soutien de 55 % des États membres, et ces pays doivent peser 65 % de la population de l'Union.
On suit également de très près ce feuilleton sur Clubic. Les Pays-Bas ont été les premiers à homologuer le système en avril, et sept autres pays ont suivi. Dans une enquête fondée sur des centaines de courriels échangés avec sept régulateurs européens, Reuters a reconstitué la campagne de pression du constructeur, et plusieurs gouvernements ont commencé à céder.

articles.title: Muse de Meta passe à la vitesse supérieure, mais l'Europe devra encore patienter
articles.summary:
Un mois à peine après son arrivée sur iPhone, Muse, l’agent IA de Meta, débarque sur iPad, à la grande joie des utilisateurs.
L’agent IA de Meta débarque sur iPad
Disponible en version macOS et iOS, Muse cartonne et pas qu’un peu : selon les estimations de Sensor Tower relayées par 9To5Mac, l’outil a, le 30 septembre dernier, dépassé les 5 millions de téléchargements. Coiffant au poteau ChatGPT, il s'est hissé au sommet du classement des applis gratuites dans l'App Store américain.
Fort de ce succès, Meta a décidé d’étendre son agent IA à d’autres appareils. La bonne nouvelle a été partagée hier sur Threads par Ivan Bruel, l’un des ingénieurs informatiques de l'entreprise : « À la demande générale, Muse est désormais disponible sur iPad ! ».
Dans la foulée, la page de l’App Store américain du service a été mise à jour : elle indique désormais qu’un appareil sous iPadOS 18.0 ou système plus récent sera nécessaire pour utiliser l’agent IA. Il sera donc possible de déléguer la gestion de ses emails et de son agenda, la réservation d’un restaurant ou le suivi de son budget à Muse, sur un écran plus grand.
D’autres nouveautés disponibles, mais une arrivée en France toujours en suspens
Meta semble bien décidée à battre le fer tant qu’il est chaud.
